subject: Polity
description: Article 280, devolution of taxes, recent commissions

questions.stem: The FINANCE COMMISSION of India is constituted under:
questions.explanation: Article 280 — every 5 years, President constitutes a Finance Commission (FC) to recommend the distribution of net tax proceeds between Union and States, and among States. CAG — Art 148. EC — Art 324. Official language — Art 343.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CHAIRMAN of the 15th Finance Commission (which covered FY 2021-22 to 2025-26) was:
questions.explanation: N. K. Singh — chaired 15th FC (formed Nov 2017). Recommended 41% vertical devolution (reduced from 42% to account for J&K becoming UT). Y. V. Reddy chaired the 14th. Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC (constituted Dec 2023).
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Advisory — tabled in Parliament along with an Action Taken Report

questions.explanation: FC recommendations are ADVISORY, not binding. Government lays them before Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on 'action taken' (ATR). In practice, most recommendations have been accepted. Chairman + 4 members have qualifications specified by Parliament.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: 'VERTICAL devolution' by the Finance Commission refers to:

options.option_text: Share of Central taxes to be transferred from Union to States collectively

questions.explanation: Vertical devolution = Union's net tax revenue share that goes to States as a group. 14th FC: 42% → 15th FC: 41% → 16th FC is determining now. HORIZONTAL devolution = how this pool is shared AMONG states (using population, area, demographic performance, income distance etc. — formula determined by the FC).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CHAIRMAN of the FIRST Finance Commission (1951) was:
questions.explanation: K. C. Neogy — chaired the 1st Finance Commission (22 November 1951). His report (Dec 1952) covered FY 1952-53 to 1956-57. C. D. Deshmukh was first Indian Governor of RBI. Chetty and Matthai were early Finance Ministers.
